page: Amazon Web Services x8i.8xlarge is a memory-intensive server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in text and image processing, with Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 10% at 2903.0. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results, reaching 34.34 GB/sec and 14.53 GB/sec respectively. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show 160.44 GB/sec for read-only operations and 72.3 GB/sec for write operations. However, text generation for large 70B LLM models is a notable performance bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 2.61 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x8i.8xlarge offers high memory density and advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations, without the added expense of GPU hardware. This makes the instance suitable for memory-heavy workloads such as in-memory databases, large-scale text processing, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing, though it is less efficient for heavy LLM text generation tasks.
